role.altitude: The agricultural inspector keeps inspecting on site, interpreting rules, explaining standards, deciding compliance and enforcement and talking with operators; collecting files before a visit, typing up paper checklists and matching paper transport documents shrink.
skills_to_grow: Working from tablet checklists on site
Checking electronic certificates and logger data
role.ambitious_version: An inspector who spends the day on site and in conversation, not typing up visits at night.

tasks.short: Prepare the visit from the establishment's file, travel, inspect agricultural commodities or operations for compliance with laws and regulations, note findings, type them into the inspection system, decide compliance and discuss findings.

steps.what: Inspector collects the establishment's file, past findings and permits before the visit
Inspector travels to the site
Inspector inspects agricultural commodities or operations for compliance with health, quality and safety regulations
Inspector notes findings on the paper checklist
Inspector types the checklist into the inspection system after the visit
Inspector decides whether the operation complies
Inspector discusses the findings with the operator

tasks.design: The inspection system shows the establishment's past findings, open actions and permits on one screen, instead of the inspector collecting files from several places. On site, findings go into a tablet checklist with the applicable regulation items. They are entered once and sync to the inspection system, instead of a paper checklist typed up after the visit. Travel, inspecting, deciding and discussing stay with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Files were collected by hand and checklists typed up after visits.
tasks.enabler_now: Inspection systems with establishment history and tablet checklists.
tasks.still_hard: Remote sites without network, where sync waits until return.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a practice that is legal on paper but unsafe in fact.

reach.learn: Whether findings arrive sooner after the visit.

evidence.claim: Pesticide users must record product, time, dose, area and crop, and move paper records to machine-readable form within 30 days for uses from 1 January 2026.
Tablet checklists that sync to a records system replace paper forms typed up later.

assumptions: Boundary: inspecting operations on site; writing reports and advising corrective action (task 14851) and collecting samples (task 14849) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: establishment history held in the inspection system for about 70% of establishments; s1 is priced at that share.
s5 saves the second entry of the paper checklist; s4 keeps its time because entry on the tablet takes about as long as on paper.
Travel, inspecting, deciding and discussing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of inspections at sites without network.
research_questions: Are findings recorded on the day of the visit?

incremental.description: No new work: the agency keeps the tablet checklist and the establishment history; syncing is automatic.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many remote sites without connection, so about half the checklists are still typed up and paper files collected (4.8); high: history for about 70% of establishments and synced checklists (9.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up regulations, interpret and enforce government acts and regulations, explain required standards to agricultural workers, answer operator questions, decide enforcement, draft the notice, have it approved, send it and follow up.

steps.what: Inspector looks up the regulation text and interpretation guidance

loop.input: The inspector's question, the regulations and the agency's interpretation notes.
loop.output: An answer with links to the articles and notes it used.
loop.check: The inspector opens each linked article and the interpretation note and checks that they say what the answer claims for this case; when they do not, or the question is new, the inspector reads the texts in full or asks the legal team.
loop.stop: Questions without a linked article are researched by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules are spread over EU and national texts and guidance.

steps.what: Inspector interprets how the acts and regulations apply to the operation
Inspector explains required standards to agricultural workers on site
Inspector answers operator questions by phone and mail
Inspector decides the enforcement action
Inspector drafts the enforcement notice, retyping operator details and findings
Supervisor checks and approves the final enforcement notice
Inspector sends the enforcement notice to the operator
Inspector follows up on compliance on site

approvals.approved_version: The enforcement notice with its findings, legal basis and deadline exactly as approved by the supervisor in s7, sent to the operator named in it; any change needs a new approval.

tasks.design: An answer desk over the regulations and the agency's interpretation notes answers the inspector's questions with article links. Published guidance pages for operators answer common questions, so fewer reach the inspector. The enforcement notice template fills operator details and findings from the inspection record. The supervisor approves the final notice before the inspector sends it. Interpreting, explaining standards on site, deciding enforcement and follow-up stay with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules were looked up across texts and notices retyped from the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Answers with article links, operator guidance pages and notice templates.
tasks.still_hard: New rules without agency interpretation yet.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a rule so a farmer sees why it protects their own herd.
tasks.altitude: Less looking up and retyping; explaining and enforcing stay.

reach.learn: Whether they find answers before the visit.

evidence.claim: An answer desk drafting only from approved texts, each answer citing its source, suits routine rule questions.

assumptions: Boundary: interpreting, explaining and enforcing rules; advising corrective action in reports (task 14851) and testifying (task 14868) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s4: operator guidance pages cover about 40% of common questions; s4 is priced at that share.
s6 saves retyping operator details and findings already in the record.
Supervisor time is shown in s7 and does not change.
unknowns: Number of enforcement notices per year.
research_questions: Do operator questions fall after guidance is published?

incremental.description: Inspector reports gaps in the guidance pages.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the rules are new, so answers often need the full texts and the guidance pages cover few questions (3.0); high: established rules with guidance covering about 40% of questions (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe the cleanliness and practices of establishment employees, check hygiene records, note findings, type them up, discuss with management and decide the outcome.

steps.what: Inspector observes the cleanliness and hygiene practices of establishment employees
Inspector pages through the establishment's hygiene training and cleaning logs
Inspector notes findings on the paper checklist
Inspector types the checklist into the inspection system after the visit
Inspector discusses findings with management
Inspector decides the outcome of the hygiene inspection

tasks.design: Establishments that keep hygiene training and cleaning logs digitally share a summary view of gaps and missed entries, instead of the inspector paging through binders. Findings go into a tablet checklist that syncs to the inspection system, instead of a paper checklist typed up later. Findings name practices, not individual employees. Observing, discussing and deciding stay with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Logs were paged through in binders and checklists typed up later.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital hygiene logs and tablet checklists.
tasks.still_hard: Establishments that keep only paper logs.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a worker skipping handwashing when the line speeds up.

reach.learn: Whether gaps are found before the visit.

evidence.claim: Tablet checklists that sync to a records system replace paper forms typed up later.

assumptions: Boundary: inspecting employee cleanliness and practices; monitoring sanitary conditions of meat plants (task 14853) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: about 50% of establishments keep digital hygiene logs; s2 is priced at that share.
s4 saves the second entry of the paper checklist.
Observing, discussing and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of establishments with digital logs.
research_questions: Are findings recorded on the day of the visit?

incremental.description: No new work: establishments keep their own digital logs, and the agency keeps the tablet checklist.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few establishments keep digital logs and many checklists are still typed up (2.6); high: about half keep digital logs and checklists sync (5.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check transport certificates and documents, inspect vehicles, containers and handling, read temperature logger data, note and type up findings, decide whether transportation and handling procedures meet regulatory requirements, and discuss with the transporter.

steps.what: Inspector matches paper certificates and consignment notes against the load
Inspector inspects vehicles, containers, loading and handling procedures
Inspector reads temperature logger data and checks it against limits
Inspector notes findings on the paper checklist
Inspector types the checklist into the inspection system after the visit
Inspector decides whether transportation and handling procedures meet regulatory requirements
Inspector discusses findings with the transporter or handler

tasks.design: Where certificates and consignment data are issued electronically, the inspector checks them in the official system on a tablet against the load, instead of matching paper copies. Logger data are downloaded and compared with the temperature limits, and excursions are flagged. Findings go into a tablet checklist that syncs, instead of being typed up later. Inspecting vehicles and handling, deciding and discussing stay with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper certificates were matched by hand and logger curves read by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic certificates, logger downloads with limit checks and tablet checklists.
tasks.still_hard: Consignments from countries without electronic certificates.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a load was handled roughly despite clean documents.

reach.learn: Whether checks take less time at the roadside.

evidence.claim: Electronic certificates for consignments can be checked in official systems instead of on paper.

assumptions: Boundary: verifying transport and handling; monitoring quarantine and treatment of plants (task 14860) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: about 60% of consignments carry electronic certificates; s1 is priced at that share.
s5 saves the second entry of the paper checklist.
Inspecting, deciding and discussing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of consignments with electronic certificates.
research_questions: Do document checks at the roadside get shorter?

incremental.description: No new work: certificates come from the official system and logger limits are set by the agency.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most consignments still carry paper certificates and many loggers cannot be downloaded on site (6.7); high: about 60% electronic certificates and downloadable loggers (12.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
